mainTopic: Mourning practices of תשעה באב (work, eating, turning over the bed) and why ט״ו באב was a day of joy
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of how רבי יהודה בר אילעי ate his last meal before תשעה באב: he sat in the lowliest spot in the house, like a mourner. Next comes a משנה on doing work on תשעה באב. It depends on local custom, but תלמידי חכמים never work, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says everyone should act like a תלמיד חכם. Several ברייתות stress how serious the day is. Eating on it is compared to eating on יום הכפורים, and work done that day brings no blessing. Only those who mourn for ירושלים will see its future joy. The גמרא then discusses רבי יהודה's view that the bed must be turned over on תשעה באב. After a back-and-forth about who is able to do it and about the other beds in the house, רבא rules that the חכמים rejected רבי יהודה completely. Finally, the גמרא asks why ט״ו באב was one of the happiest days for ישראל. It brings several answers: the tribes were allowed to marry each other, בנימין was let back in, the deaths in the מדבר ended, and the road guards of ירבעם were removed. עולא's account continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the story of the mourner's last meal
steps.stepSummary: The story of רבי יהודה בר אילעי ends: he sat between the oven and the stove, ate dry bread with a jug of water, and looked like someone whose dead relative was lying in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would sit between the oven and the stove and eat. He drank a jug of water with the bread, and he looked like a person whose dead relative was lying in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that started on the previous page about how רבי יהודה בר אילעי ate his last meal before תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail shows mourning. He sat in the least honored spot in the house, ate plain food, and drank only water. The point is that the meal before the fast should feel like a mourner's meal, not a festive one.

keyTerms.meaning: Stove (a cooking range); the space between oven and stove was the lowliest spot in the house
His dead relative is lying before him, not yet buried; the deepest stage of mourning

phrases.english: between the oven and the stove, and he would eat,
phrases.notes: This finishes a story from the previous page about רבי יהודה בר אילעי's last meal before תשעה באב.

phrases.english: and he would drink a jug of water with it,
and he looked like one whose dead relative is lying before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last meal before תשעה באב should be eaten in the manner of a mourner.

steps.title: Doing work on the Ninth of Av depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that doing work on תשעה באב follows local custom, but תלמידי חכמים never work on that day. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says every person should act like a תלמיד חכם on this.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: In a place where people usually work on תשעה באב, they may work. In a place where people usually do not work, they do not work. And everywhere, תלמידי חכמים stop working. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A person should always treat himself like a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about whether one may do work (מלאכה) on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike eating, which is clearly forbidden, doing work on תשעה באב is not fully forbidden; it depends on the custom of each place. Still, תלמידי חכמים always hold back. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further and says everyone should hold himself to that higher standard.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people have the custom

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying work on תשעה באב is fully forbidden like eating. The basic rule follows local custom; the stricter practice is for תלמידי חכמים, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל recommends it for everyone.

phrases.english: We learned in a mishna there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in מסכת פסחים.

phrases.english: In a place where they were accustomed to do work
on the Ninth of Av, they do work;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת — אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.english: in a place where they were accustomed not to do work, they do not do work.
And in every place, Torah scholars are idle.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה כָּל אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.english: A person should always make himself like a Torah scholar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meal before the fast to the question of working on the day itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work on תשעה באב follows local custom; תלמידי חכמים always refrain, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says everyone should act like them.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and gives his reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view and adds the reason: so that the person will truly feel the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, a person should always treat himself like a תלמיד חכם, so that he will feel the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds something new: the reason. If a person is busy working, he is distracted and does not feel the hunger and sadness of the day. Not working makes the fast truly felt.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this; a supporting source
So that he will fast (truly feel the fast)

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם,
phrases.english: A person should always make himself like a Torah scholar,
so that he will fast.
phrases.notes: Without work to distract him, he really feels the hunger and sadness of the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the last line of the משנה in step 2 and adds its reason.
steps.raayaObject: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view that everyone should refrain from work like a תלמיד חכם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל with the added reason כדי שיתענה.

steps.title: Eating on the Ninth of Av is like eating on יום הכפורים; work brings no blessing
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says eating and drinking on תשעה באב is like doing so on יום הכפורים. רבי עקיבא says whoever works on תשעה באב will never see a sign of blessing from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, whoever eats and drinks on תשעה באב, it is as if he ate and drank on יום הכפורים. רבי עקיבא says: whoever does work on תשעה באב will never see a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with two strong statements about how serious תשעה באב is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל compares the fast of תשעה באב, which comes from the נביאים, to the Torah fast of יום הכפורים, to show how seriously it must be taken. רבי עקיבא focuses on work: even where it is allowed, any money earned that day will not bring blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement, a Torah-level fast

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Whoever eats and drinks on the Ninth of Av,
it is as if he eats and drinks on Yom Kippur.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Whoever does work on the Ninth of Av
never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more sources stressing the seriousness of תשעה באב, both for eating and for work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating on תשעה באב is treated as gravely as eating on יום הכפורים; work done that day brings no blessing.

steps.title: Only those who mourn for ירושלים will see its joy
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that whoever works on תשעה באב and does not mourn for ירושלים will not see its future joy, learned from a פסוק in ישעיהו. From this comes the rule: mourners for ירושלים will see its joy, and non-mourners will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: whoever does work on תשעה באב and does not mourn for ירושלים will not see her joy, as the פסוק says: "Rejoice with ירושלים and be glad with her, all who love her; rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn for her." From here they said: whoever mourns for ירושלים will merit to see her joy, and whoever does not mourn for her will not see her joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the view of the חכמים, who explain what is wrong with working on תשעה באב and bring a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים connect work to a lack of mourning: someone who goes on with business as usual is not mourning for ירושלים. The פסוק says those who mourn for her will rejoice with her, so those who do not mourn lose that future joy.

keyTerms.meaning: In her joy (the future rebuilding of ירושלים)
As it is said (introducing a פסוק)
From here they said; a general rule drawn from the source

steps.whatToRemember: Mourning for ירושלים now is the key to seeing its joy later; going about ordinary work on תשעה באב shows a lack of that mourning.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that whoever mourns for ירושלים will merit to see its joy became a well-known and widely quoted principle.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Whoever does work on the Ninth of Av
and does not mourn for Jerusalem
will not see her joy,
as it is said: "Rejoice with Jerusalem
and be glad with her, all who love her;
rejoice greatly with her,
all who mourn for her."
From here they said:
Whoever mourns for Jerusalem
merits and sees her joy,
and one who does not mourn for Jerusalem
does not see her joy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a third view, adding a פסוק-based reason about mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever mourns for ירושלים merits to see her joy; whoever works on תשעה באב without mourning does not.

steps.title: Eating meat and drinking wine on the Ninth of Av is condemned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the theme: whoever eats meat and drinks wine on תשעה באב is described by the פסוק "and their sins are upon their bones."
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: whoever eats meat and drinks wine on תשעה באב, about him the פסוק says: "And their sins were upon their bones."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא supporting the idea that a person must act like a mourner on תשעה באב, this time about eating meat and wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and wine are foods of celebration. Eating them in connection with תשעה באב shows the opposite of mourning, so the ברייתא applies a harsh פסוק from יחזקאל to such a person.
steps.confusionAlert: Eating anything on the day itself is already forbidden, so this is understood as the last meal before the fast begins, which ties back to the story in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches one idea: on תשעה באב, and even at the meal before it, a person should behave like a mourner for ירושלים.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹכֵל בָּשָׂר וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב —
phrases.english: Whoever eats meat and drinks wine on the Ninth of Av,
phrases.notes: This means the last meal before the fast, since eating at all on the day is already forbidden.

phrases.english: about him the verse says:
"And their sins were upon their bones."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a supporting ברייתא to the theme of mourning in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that one must act as a mourner for ירושלים in connection with תשעה באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא applying the פסוק in יחזקאל 32:27 to one who eats meat and drinks wine on תשעה באב.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about turning over the bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי יהודה requires turning over the bed on תשעה באב, and the חכמים did not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה requires a person to turn over the bed, but the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning over the bed is something a mourner does. רבי יהודה wants people to do it on תשעה באב too, as a sign of mourning for ירושלים. The חכמים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Turning over the bed, a sign of mourning
They did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda requires turning over the bed,
but the Rabbis did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mourning themes of earlier steps to a new line in the משנה about turning over the bed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires turning over the bed on תשעה באב; the חכמים disagree.

steps.title: What about pregnant and nursing women?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that the חכמים challenged רבי יהודה: his rule seems impossible for pregnant and nursing women.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: The חכמים said to רבי יהודה: According to you, what will happen to pregnant women and nursing women?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי יהודה's rule. If the bed is turned over, people must sleep on the floor, and pregnant or nursing women cannot do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is practical: a rule that applies to everyone would force weak people into real hardship. This suggests the rule cannot be right as a blanket requirement.

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
According to your words, pregnant women and nursing women,
what will become of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's rule from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's requirement to turn over the bed on תשעה באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone must turn over the bed, pregnant and nursing women would be forced to sleep on the floor, which they cannot do.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: I only meant people who are able
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that his rule was only for those who are able to sleep without a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too only said it about someone who is able.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the challenge by limiting his rule. It only applies to people who can handle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not drop his rule. He explains it was never meant for weak people like pregnant or nursing women. So the challenge does not hurt his position.

phrases.english: He said to them: I too
only said it about one who is able.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְּיָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to require everyone, even weak people, to turn over the bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule only applies to people who are able to sleep without a bed.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: both sides agree on able and unable
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא supports this: רבי יהודה agrees about someone who cannot, and the חכמים agree about someone who can.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught like this: רבי יהודה agrees with the חכמים about someone who is not able, and the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about someone who is able.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that backs up what רבי יהודה just said. It shows both sides agree in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone unable does not turn over the bed, says רבי יהודה too. Someone able does, say the חכמים too. Now it sounds like there is no argument left, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
About someone who is not able

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לַחֲכָמִים בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda agrees with the Rabbis about one who is not able,
and the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Yehuda about one who is able.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 9 with another ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's rule is limited to people who are able
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that each side agrees with the other in one case

steps.title: So what do they still argue about?
steps.stepSummary: Since both sides agree in both cases, the גמרא asks what the real difference between them is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. If they agree about able and unable people, where is the argument?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly says they disagree, but the ברייתא makes it sound like they agree on everything. The גמרא needs to find the point where they still differ.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 10, which seemed to erase the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical point on which רבי יהודה and the חכמים still disagree.

steps.title: The difference: the other beds in the house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that they argue about the other beds in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the other beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about whether you must also turn over the other beds in the house, not just your own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an able person, both sides agree something is done with the bed. The disagreement is how far it goes: רבי יהודה requires all the beds in the house to be turned over, the way a mourner does.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: The difference between them is the other beds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about the other beds in the house.

steps.title: Source: a mourner turns over all the beds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that when a mourner turns over the bed, he turns over all the beds, not just his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: When they said to turn over the bed, he does not turn over only his own bed, but he turns over all the beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain where the idea of "other beds" comes from. A real mourner turns over every bed in the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that turning over beds normally includes all the beds. So the argument in step 12 makes sense: רבי יהודה follows the full mourner's practice on תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: When they said to turn over the bed,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a mourner after a death.

phrases.english: he does not turn over only his own bed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל הַמִּטּוֹת כּוּלָּן הוּא כּוֹפֶה.
phrases.english: rather he turns over all the beds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the answer in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That turning over beds can mean all the beds in the house
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the practice of a mourner

steps.title: רבא: the הלכה follows our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like our משנה: the חכמים did not agree with רבי יהודה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is like the תנא of our משנה, and the חכמים did not agree with him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final ruling. We follow the plain words of our משנה, where the חכמים simply disagree with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא said the חכמים agree in the case of someone able. רבא rejects that and rules that the חכמים disagree completely, even for someone able. So there is no requirement to turn over the bed on תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, the author of our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the bed is not turned over on תשעה באב. רבא rules like our משנה, where the חכמים fully reject רבי יהודה's requirement.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't follow the second ברייתא here. It said the חכמים agree in the case of someone able, but רבא rules that they did not agree at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for how we behave on תשעה באב.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halakha is like our tanna,
phrases.notes: He means the תנא of our משנה, who simply wrote that the חכמים did not agree.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis did not agree with him at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling and sets aside the agreement described in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows our משנה: the חכמים fully disagree with רבי יהודה, so the bed is not turned over on תשעה באב.

steps.title: The happiest days: ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה: no days were as happy for ישראל as ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: There were no days as happy for ישראל as the fifteenth of Av and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting another line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the sad laws of תשעה באב, the משנה turns to joyful days. Calling יום הכפורים, a fast day, one of the happiest days is surprising, and so is ט״ו באב, which is not a known holiday.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There were no days as happy for the Jewish people
as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the bed discussion ended in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים were the happiest days for ישראל.

steps.title: We understand why יום הכפורים is happy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a question: יום הכפורים makes sense as a happy day, because it brings forgiveness and is the day the second לוחות were given.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for יום הכפורים, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day the last לוחות were given.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It first explains why יום הכפורים is happy, so it can ask next why ט״ו באב is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means "we understand this part." יום הכפורים is happy because sins are forgiven and the second לוחות were given on it. The unspoken problem is ט״ו באב, which the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, we understand this part (sets up a question about another part)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first half of the question. בשלמא explains the easy part; the real question about ט״ו באב comes right after.

phrases.english: It makes sense for Yom Kippur —
because it has pardon and forgiveness,
the day on which the last tablets were given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins asking about the statement in step 15 by first explaining the part that makes sense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Having explained יום הכפורים, the גמרא is preparing to ask what makes ט״ו באב a happy day.

steps.title: What was special about the fifteenth of Av?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question: יום הכפורים makes sense, but why was ט״ו באב such a happy day?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the fifteenth of Av, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the question it began in the last step. It asks what happened on ט״ו באב that made it so joyful. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed why יום הכפורים is joyful: it brings forgiveness, and the second לוחות were given on it. The word אֶלָּא, meaning 'but,' sets ט״ו באב against that, because no clear reason for celebrating it has been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The fifteenth day of the month of Av (ט״ו באב)
What is it? A request to explain something

phrases.english: But the fifteenth of Av,
what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question started in step 16 by contrasting ט״ו באב with יום הכפורים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The historical event that made ט״ו באב a day of great joy.

steps.title: שמואל: the tribes were allowed to marry each other
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says ט״ו באב is the day the tribes were permitted to marry into one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is the day the tribes were allowed to come into one another, meaning to marry each other.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer. On ט״ו באב, people from different tribes were allowed to marry each other again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At one time, marriage between tribes had been restricted. Lifting that restriction brought the tribes back together, so the day became a celebration.

keyTerms.meaning: To come into one another, meaning to marry between tribes

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The day on which the tribes were permitted
to enter one into another.
phrases.notes: In plain words, this means marrying someone from a different tribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב is the day marriage between the tribes became permitted.

steps.title: How did they learn that the restriction ended?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the people learned from the פסוק that let them allow marriage between tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about שמואל's answer. The Torah had restricted these marriages, so what reading of the פסוק allowed them? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A restriction that comes from the Torah cannot simply be dropped. The גמרא wants to see which reading of the פסוק showed that it was only temporary.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they expound? What did they learn from the פסוק?

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind שמואל's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reading of the פסוק that limited the ban on marriage between tribes.

steps.title: The rule applied only to that generation
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'this is the matter,' they learned that the restriction applied only to the generation of the daughters of צלפחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'This is the matter which ה׳ commanded concerning the daughters of צלפחד.' They learned that this matter would apply only in this generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the word 'this' in the פסוק limits the rule. The ban on marrying out of one's tribe was meant only for that one generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban came about so that the land of בנות צלפחד would stay within their own tribe. Reading 'זֶה' as 'only this generation' meant that later generations were free, so the tribes could marry each other again.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughters of צלפחד, who inherited their father's land

phrases.english: "This is the matter that ה׳ commanded
concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, etc."
This matter shall not be practiced
except in this generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ לִבְנוֹת צְלׇפְחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by giving the reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'זֶה' limits the ban on marriage between tribes to that single generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one small word in a פסוק can mark a rule as temporary.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the tribe of בנימין was let back in
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a different answer: ט״ו באב is the day the tribe of בנימין was allowed to marry into the rest of ישראל again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב נחמן: it is the day the tribe of בנימין was allowed to enter the community. The פסוק says that the men of ישראל swore at מצפה that none of them would give his daughter to בנימין as a wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to what happened on ט״ו באב. The other tribes had sworn not to marry their daughters to בנימין, and on this day the tribe was allowed back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the joy comes from ending an oath, not a Torah law. A whole tribe that had been cut off rejoined the nation, and that made the day a celebration.

keyTerms.meaning: To enter the community, meaning to marry into the rest of ישראל
מצפה, the place where the oath was taken

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Naḥman said:
The day on which the tribe of Binyamin was permitted
to enter the congregation,
as it is stated: "And the men of Israel swore in Mitzpah,
saying: None of us
shall give his daughter to Binyamin as a wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question in step 17, different from שמואל's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב is the day the tribe of בנימין was allowed to marry into the rest of ישראל again.

steps.title: How could the oath be set aside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reading of the oath allowed them to marry into בנימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they expound?
steps.whatsHappening: The same follow-up question appears again, this time about the oath. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath is binding, so the people needed a reason to think it did not cover them. The גמרא asks what that reason was.

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב נחמן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reading of the oath that let later generations marry into בנימין.

steps.title: 'Of us,' but not 'of our children'
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the oath said 'none of us,' so it bound only the people who swore, not their children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the oath says 'of us,' and not 'of our children.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the exact wording of the oath limited it. It covered only the people who made it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath said 'אִישׁ מִמֶּנּוּ,' meaning 'none of us.' Since it did not mention children, the next generation was free to marry into בנימין.

phrases.english: Rav said:
"Of us," and not: Of our children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 with the exact wording of the oath.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oath bound only those who swore it, not their descendants.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the deaths in the desert ended
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a third answer: ט״ו באב is the day the generation of the מדבר stopped dying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is the day the deaths of the desert generation came to an end.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third, different answer to what happened on ט״ו באב. The dying of the generation in the מדבר came to an end on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer has nothing to do with marriage. It is about the end of a punishment, and the next step will explain why that ending was such a joyful event.

keyTerms.meaning: That they came to an end
The deaths of the generation in the desert

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The day on which the deaths in the wilderness ended.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ט״ו באב is the day the deaths of the desert generation came to an end.

steps.title: Once the deaths ended, ה׳ spoke to משה again
steps.stepSummary: A teaching and a פסוק show that ה׳ did not speak to משה until the desert deaths ended, which explains why their end was a joyful day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the master said: until the deaths of the desert generation ended, there was no speech with משה. The פסוק says, 'And it was, when all the men of war had finished dying, ה׳ spoke to me.' Only then did the speech come to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן's answer. It explains why the end of the deaths was so happy: ה׳ began speaking to משה again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the פסוק is the proof. First 'all the men of war finished dying,' and right after that 'ה׳ spoke to me.' This shows the speech came back only after the deaths stopped, and that renewed closeness to ה׳ is the reason for the joy.

keyTerms.meaning: Speech, ה׳ speaking to the נביא
The men of war, meaning the adult men of that generation

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three answers for ט״ו באב: the tribes could marry each other (שמואל), בנימין was allowed back in (רב נחמן), and the desert deaths ended so ה׳ spoke to משה again (רבי יוחנן). The next step adds a fourth answer from עולא.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Until the deaths in the wilderness ended,
there was no speech with Moshe,
as it is stated: "And it was, when were finished
all the men of war dying.
And ה׳ spoke to me."
Only then was the speech to me.
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads this from the order of the פסוק‎: ה׳'s speech to משה came only after the deaths were over.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר עַד שֶׁלֹּא כָּלוּ מֵתֵי מִדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer by explaining why the end of the deaths was joyful.
steps.raayaObject: That the end of the desert deaths was cause for great joy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of 'מר' together with דברים 2:16–17, which shows that ה׳'s speech to משה came back only after the deaths ended.

steps.title: עולא: the day the road guards were removed
steps.stepSummary: עולא says ט״ו באב is the day הושע בן אלה removed the guards that ירבעם בן נבט had placed on the roads to stop ישראל from going up for the רגל. The גמרא then begins to quote what הושע said.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: ט״ו באב is the day that הושע בן אלה cancelled the guards that ירבעם בן נבט had set up on the roads so that ישראל would not go up for the festival. And he said:
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives another answer to the question of what happened on ט״ו באב. It was the day King הושע בן אלה took down ירבעם's road guards. The last word, 'and he said,' sets up the next line, where we hear what הושע declared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins the list of answers from שמואל (step 18), רב נחמן (step 21) and רבי יוחנן (step 24). Each one names a different happy event on ט״ו באב. ירבעם had blocked the people from going up to ירושלים for the רגלים, and הושע בן אלה ended that block, so the people could go up again.

keyTerms.meaning: The last king of the northern kingdom of ישראל
The first king of the northern kingdom, who stopped people from going to ירושלים
Guards or guard posts placed on the roads
For the festival, going up to ירושלים on פסח, שבועות and סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence does not end here. 'וְאָמַר' means 'and he said,' and what הושע בן אלה said comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is the day on which Hoshea son of Ela cancelled
the guards that Jeroboam son of Nevat had placed

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַדְּרָכִים שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: on the roads, so that the Jewish people would not go up for the festival,
and he said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth answer to the question in step 17, after שמואל, רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן, for why ט״ו באב was a joyful day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened on ט״ו באב that made it a day of joy?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the day הושע בן אלה removed ירבעם בן נבט's road guards that stopped ישראל from going up for the רגל.
